To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cold acclimation of winter wheat is accompanied by a transient disassembly of microtubules, that this disassembly may be a trigger for cold-induced growth arrest and cold acclimation, and that it may be a part of a mechanism that is involved in the sensing of a low temperature stress.
cold acclimation is accompanied by a transient microtubule depolymerization that may be involved in the induction of freezing tolerance in winter wheat.
microtubule dynamics are involved in the sensing of cold stress and the subsequent development of freezing tolerance in wheat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether microtubule (MT) disassembly is a trigger for the induction of freezing tolerance.
a role for microtubule dynamics in cold acclimation.
the question of whether a transient partial disassembly of the microtubule cytoskeleton may trigger the cold-acclimation process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
microtubule dynamics are involved in the perception and/or transduction of the cold signal in the tolerant cultivar.
the microtubule system plays a role in cold acclimation.
microtubule dynamics are involved in the sensing of cold stress, but the role of microtubes in the cold acclimation process itself remains to be elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cold-stable microfilaments and microtubules are not the result of the cold stress, but are rather a result of the cold acclimation.
the cold-induced microtubule reorganization is not a consequence of the freezing tolerance, but rather a trigger for its induction.
cold-induced microtubule depolymerization is not only a consequence of cold acclimation, but also a trigger of the cold acclimation process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the disassembly of microtubules is not only a response to cold stress, but also a prerequisite for cold acclimatization.
microtubule assembly is an important factor in cold acclimation and that a transient partial disassembly may trigger cold acclimation.
microtubule assembly/disassembly is an integral part of cold stress response and that microtubules may be a sensor of low-temperature stresses.
